advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten the failover trigger_tokens (e.g. drop or qualify bare `timeout`/`Permanent`/`Transient`) so the content trigger does not fire on unrelated diffs.
evidence: registry.py:634 `if oid not in fired and any(tok in body for tok in tokens):` — literal substring match, no word boundary/case guard
Comparable committed `_CONCURRENCY_TOKENS` (registry.py:418) deliberately use disambiguating suffixes like `Lock(`, `Thread(`, `Task.Run(` to avoid exactly this over-firing
advisory.finding: The failover overlay's `trigger_tokens` include broad, case-sensitive substrings (`timeout`, `fallback`, `fall back`, `Permanent`, `Transient`) matched with plain substring semantics (`tok in body`, no word boundaries), so the overlay will content-fire on many unrelated diffs (e.g. any line mentioning `--timeout`, `socket.timeout`, a `Permanently`/`Transient` word in comments or config). Because it is advisory this costs an extra pass rather than a wrong verdict, but the low precision undercuts the trigger's value.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add negative-control tests for the `failover` content trigger: a context-only token line and a benign token-free diff must NOT fire, matching the coverage the `concurrency` overlay already has.
evidence: Only positive test added: tests/unit/test_code_review_triggers.py:165 `def test_failover_committed_token_fires_on_fallback_diff():` asserting `"failover" in reg.content_triggered_overlays(diff)` for an added `should_fall_back(` line

Sibling concurrency ships negative controls the failover overlay lacks: test_code_review_triggers.py:186 `test_async_await_only_diff_does_not_fire_concurrency` and :197 `test_context_line_only_token_does_not_fire_concurrency`

New broad trigger tokens added in criteria_routing.json:172-180: `fallback`, `fall back`, `timeout`, `Recoverable`, `Transient`, `Permanent` (case-sensitive substrings matched against `+`/`-` line bodies via the added `_scan_packaged_tokens` at registry.py:638)
ABSENCE: no test asserts `"failover" not in reg.content_triggered_overlays(diff)` for a benign token-free diff, a context-only-line token, or an unrelated substring hit such as `request_timeout = 30`
advisory.finding: The new `failover` content-trigger has only a single positive test and no negative control, so it cannot detect over-firing on its broad substring tokens. The sibling `concurrency` overlay ships two negative controls (context-only line must not fire; deliberately-excluded family must not fire), but no equivalent exists for `failover`. Named violating input: a diff adding `+    request_timeout = 30` (an unrelated config knob) matches the `timeout` token and fires the failover overlay, and a diff whose token appears only on an unchanged CONTEXT line would be expected NOT to fire — neither boundary is asserted, so a regression in the packaged-token scan (`_scan_packaged_tokens`/`_scan_token_map`) is invisible.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add tests asserting `"failover" not in reg.content_triggered_overlays(diff)` for (1) a diff whose only failover token sits on an unchanged context line, and (2) a benign diff with no failover vocabulary; optionally assert intended firing/non-firing for a broad substring like `timeout` on an unrelated config line.
